concept: Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore
summary: Source-anchored research for Automated Embedding (autoEmbed) quantization types including binaryNoRescore. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Independent background evidence: the Hugging Face/mixedbread quantization experiment reports roughly 92.5% retained retrieval performance without binary rescoring versus about 96% with rescoring. It uses float-query/binary-document rescoring, so these figures do not benchmark Atlas binaryNoRescore or its full-precision rescoring alternative. (low confidence)
The autoEmbed quantization field accepts float, scalar, binary, and binaryNoRescore; scalar is the default. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
For autoEmbed, float stores 32-bit values. Scalar uses model-provided int8 values and approximately one quarter of float embedding storage and RAM. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

For autoEmbed, binary indexes one-bit values but retains full-precision vectors for candidate rescoring. MongoDB states RAM use is about 1/24 of float; this is not a corresponding total disk-storage reduction. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

binaryNoRescore uses model-provided one-bit vectors without rescoring. MongoDB describes faster queries and lower storage cost than binary, with lower accuracy; it gives no universal latency or recall improvement. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
MongoDB server documentation lists default similarity as dotProduct for float, cosine for scalar, and euclidean for binary and binaryNoRescore. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Mongoid auto_embed_field accepts quantization and passes it into the autoEmbed index field specification. DRIVERS-3389 tracks the builder/type support required to expose these index options through language drivers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-24)

Scope boundary: Percona documents a self-managed autoEmbed pipeline whose Ollama model catalog sets quantization to float. This is evidence of a separate implementation context, not verification of Atlas binaryNoRescore support or performance. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)
